extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers, HIV researchers, and clinical/translational investigators preparing or evaluating NIH K/R-type proposals
extracted.subtask_description: A K08 research strategy describing three specific aims to determine whether HIV latent reservoir (LR) size or inducibility correlate with suboptimal immune recovery on ART and whether cytokine therapies alter the LR, including assay choice, cohort selection, power calculations, and RCR/institutional support plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of suboptimal immune responders (SoIRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: SoIRs are defined here as HIV-1-infected individuals who began a period of viral suppression with an absolute CD4 count < 200 cells/μL and had a CD4 count < 350 after 5 years of viral suppression, during which viral loads (VLs) were measured to be < 200 copies/mL or < limit of detection (LOD) at least every 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition was chosen to mirror published morbidity/mortality studies and to maximize participant-finding in collaborating cohorts; used to exclude virologic failure as cause of poor immune recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of control group
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls are HIV-1-infected individuals who began a period of viral suppression with CD4 < 200 and had a CD4 count > 500 after 5 years of viral suppression, during which viral loads were measured to be < 200 copies/mL or < LOD at least every 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls will be matched to identified SoIRs by age (within 7 yrs), sex, race, and nadir CD4 count (within 50 cells/μL), and where possible, also by HCV and CMV co-infection status and ever/never intravenous drug use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of viral suppression / virologic failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Viral suppression is defined as < 200 copies/mL in keeping with AIDS Clinical Trials Group definitions of virologic failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a standard ACTG cutoff ensures consistency with prior studies and exclusion of virologic failure as a confounder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for measuring the latent reservoir (LR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the LR at 1-2 years after the start of ART because the HIV LR is stable after approximately 12 months on suppressive ART.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing >=1 year avoids measuring fast-decaying LR populations and selects a timepoint that reflects the stable, persistent reservoir for prediction of later immune recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the intact proviral DNA assay (IPDA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPDA separately quantifies the frequency of intact and defective HIV proviruses in a population of cells via duplex droplet digital PCR technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPDA requires 10 times fewer input cells than QVOA, can be run in 1-2 days, works on cryopreserved samples and lymphoid tissue, and provides a definitive maximal estimate of the LR by quantifying intact proviruses (not just induced ones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quantitative viral outgrowth assay (QVOA) when sample abundant
rubrics_metrics.description: QVOA provides a definitive minimal estimate of the LR but is labor-intensive, requires a large number of cells, and takes 2-3 weeks to complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples with > 10M resting CD4s will also be tested by QVOA to obtain a minimal functional estimate of inducible replication-competent proviruses; QVOA remains a gold-standard comparator despite throughput limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of the inducibility index
rubrics_metrics.description: The inducibility index is the frequency of intact induced HIV RNA in CD4s divided by the frequency of intact HIV DNA in the same sample (calculated for both in vivo and ex vivo measurements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalizing HIV induction to the number of intact proviruses distinguishes higher transcriptional activity per intact provirus (inducibility) from simply having a larger LR; used to compare SoIRs vs controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and characteristics of the quantitative viral induction assay (QVIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: QVIA is an ex vivo limiting-dilution assay developed to measure ex vivo HIV induction from latency and can potentially distinguish transcription from intact proviruses versus transcription-competent but defective proviruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QVIA requires many fewer input cells than QVOA, takes two days to complete, and establishes qPCR cutoffs to discriminate low-RNA wells (defective proviruses). If cell numbers are limiting, TILDA (requires ~1M resting CD4s) may be substituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study population selection and cohort sources
rubrics_metrics.description: SoIRs and controls will be identified from four collaborating clinical cohorts: SCOPE (UCSF), Johns Hopkins HIV Clinical Cohort (JHHCC), Cleveland Immune Failure (CLIF) cohort, and ACTG ALLRT; if needed, expanded to MACS or CNICS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using multiple large cohorts with stored cryopreserved PBMCs, biopsies, and clinical data increases ability to find matched cases/controls and to access sufficient cells and tissue types (blood, lymph node, gut).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching and control of confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls matched to SoIRs by age (within 7 years), sex, race, nadir CD4 (within 50 cells/μL), and when possible HCV/CMV co-infection status and IV drug use history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching helps control for known risk factors for suboptimal immune recovery and isolates association between LR metrics and immune outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and power considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the relative group effect method and varying coefficient of variation (k), required sample sizes per group to detect a difference in LR size with 80% power at alpha=0.05 are given (k=1 → n=30; k=1.5 → n=52; k=2 → n=70).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Varying assumed variance (k) reflects uncertainty in IPDA variance among SoIRs; study is powered to detect correlations within a subpopulation of SoIRs given these sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for timing confounders (nadir CD4 and time on ART)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous studies did not control for CD4 nadir or time on ART; this study will control for these variables in comparisons between SoIRs and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting for nadir and ART duration is critical because they independently influence immune recovery and bias associations between LR measures and CD4 outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of cell type for LR measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the LR primarily in resting CD4+ T cells (where the latent reservoir resides); lymphoid tissue and gut biopsies will be used for tissue LR assessment when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resting CD4s capture the reservoir relevant to latency; IPDA can be run on cryopreserved resting CD4s and tissue-derived cells, enabling comparisons across compartments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay validation, controls, and sequence-informed primer/probe design
rubrics_metrics.description: IPDA primer/probe sets were selected after mining near full-length proviral sequence data to maximize capture of intact proviruses while quantifying deletions and APOBEC-mediated hypermutation; control experiments use proviral constructs with specific defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assay design and published validation experiments (e.g., control constructs, demonstration of dynamic range) are required to show discriminatory capacity and to justify interpretation of intact vs defective counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated results framing and downstream application
rubrics_metrics.description: If LR size or inducibility correlate with suboptimal immune response, the LR could be a clinically meaningful biomarker enabling early identification of patients at risk and informing interventions; null or descriptive results still inform therapeutic targeting and assay ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear articulation of expected outcomes supports translational rationale and future grant planning (e.g., R01 proposals, informing cytokine therapy trials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential problems and alternative strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: If insufficient SoIRs/controls are found in collaborating cohorts, expand search to additional cohorts (MACS, CNICS); if insufficient cells for QVIA, use TILDA which requires fewer cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specified contingency plans for limited sample availability or assay input ensure feasibility and maintain study aims despite practical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses for Aims (explicit evaluative expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothesis 1: LR size measured in blood and lymphoid tissue is positively correlated with suboptimal immune response. Hypothesis 2: Infected CD4+ T cells of SoIRs have increased HIV induction from latency when normalized for LR size. Hypothesis 3: Exogenous IL-7 and IL-15 lead to an increase in LR size by favoring proliferation of CD4+ T cells over latency reactivation; exogenous IL-2 leads to a decrease in LR due to stronger latency-inducing effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These hypotheses define the primary scientific questions and the directional expectations against which data and statistical tests will be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for assessing cytokine therapy effects on LR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cryopreserved PBMCs from clinical trials of IL-2, IL-7, and IL-15 to measure intact and defective proviruses in CD4s via IPDA before and after cytokine administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because samples are banked, sample size is fixed; analyses must account for this limitation and focus on within-subject pre/post comparisons where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor & Reproducibility: methodological transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe isolation of resting CD4+ T cells from viably stored PBMCs and lymphatic tissue and performance of IPDA as previously described; include assay protocols, controls, and prior generation of sequence datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing methods, preliminary data, and references to validated protocols supports reproducibility and reviewer assessment of technical feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training plan compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan follows NIH Policy on Instruction in the Responsible Conduct of Research covering five instructional components: Format, Subject Matter, Faculty Participation, Duration of Instruction, and Frequency of Instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: incorporate face-to-face discussions (Research Integrity Colloquia, Department meetings), cover conflict of interest, human subjects, authorship, mentoring, etc., involve faculty mentors, exceed suggested 8 contact hours over award, include 2-3 formal contact hours per year and recertification every 4 years; engagement with National Research Mentoring Network planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and resource availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Johns Hopkins environment provides laboratory space (Siliciano Lab), BSL-3, personal office/bench space, droplet digital PCR system and ddPCR setup room, CFAR cores (administrative, developmental, clinical, prevention, laboratory), and multiple institutional programs to support junior investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting available equipment, core services, mentorship, and institutional programs (K-to-R, ICTR support, pilot funding, biostatistical consults) demonstrates feasibility and institutional commitment required for successful project execution.
